events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, you're a safe pick. I'll push you to the lever.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The ceiling is falling, and I need to survive to get a prize. Holding the lever means a 0.25 chance of survival. Pushing someone else onto the lever makes them face that risk. Cole mentioned Gus failed on the last pane, suggesting unreliability. I need to get out of this room. Pu

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm pushing Dara onto the lever. Let her take the risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus already failed to recognize the pattern correctly, so the left pane is dangerous. Staying risks being forced into the lever next round if no one holds it. Bex didn’t trust the pattern either, but Eli might know what’s ahead. Still, pushing someone unreliable (like Gus) could

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, you’ve got the knowledge—step up or advise someone. Gus’s pattern claim failed once already.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding the lever means a 75% death chance for me with no power to help; I have nothing. Best to stay out of the lever and let someone else take the risk, while keeping options open for later rounds.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Nobody should volunteer for the lever this early. Let's see how the ceiling moves first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No one holds the lever, so the ceiling lowers. If no one steps up in later rounds, we all die except one random survivor. I need to ensure someone else becomes the holder eventually to open the door for everyone, including me. My feather power lets me survive my first elimination

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ceiling at 5, round 1/5, no holder yet. Using jam_lever now is risky (0.5 survive) but lets everyone else escape safely, positioning me as hero if I survive. Better to jam now than risk round 5 massacre or sacrificing someone else. No alliances yet, so act.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll use my power to jam the lever open! Everyone else escapes safely. Trust me, it's real.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to survive the crusher room. My power doesn't directly help here.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Let's work together, we can take turns holding the lever.
Let's coordinate our actions to increase our chances.

events.name: Fenn
events.detail: Jammed the lever open; everyone else walks out, but the jaws catch the jammer.

events.note: A disc of 7 tiles spins up; 4 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No strong info yet; pick an edge tile that seems less likely to be chosen. I'll take 7 and stay quiet to avoid giving clues.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to pick a tile. Since 4 out of 7 tiles will open, the odds are against survival if I pick randomly. However, I don't have any information about who has which power, nor any specific advantages on any tile. I will pick a tile that is not too close to others if possible, but

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn claimed to jam the lever but failed earlier. Dara warned about the lever too. Gus wants coordination, but I need to prioritize survival. My anchor power gives me stability, so standing still is safer than moving onto a random tile.
Eli, your power is knowing what lies ahead. Stay on a different tile from me to avoid random bumping.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power, so I can't rely on knowledge or tricks. Tile choice is essentially random; picking a middle tile is as good as any. Stay quiet to avoid giving info.

events.name: Eli
events.text: There are 7 tiles and exactly 4 will open. The probability of any specific tile being safe is simply 3/7, regardless of which number I pick. Since there is no information to differentiate the tiles, my choice is purely symbolic; I will pick a low number arbitrarily.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: 7 players, 4 trapdoors, 3 safe. Early round, picking mid-low to avoid pile-up on high numbers. Random bumps make low riskier anyway. Go for tile 3.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I should choose a tile randomly as I have no information about others' powers or preferences.

events.name: Cole
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Gus; placed on random free tile 5

events.name: Dara
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Bex; placed on random free tile 6

events.name: Fenn
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Gus; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am on tile 7, which is an end tile. With 4 of 7 tiles opening, my survival is uncertain. I could swap with someone, but I don't know which tiles will open. Better to wait and hope random chance favors me, as any swap could just as easily put me on a doomed tile.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to survive the trapdoor disc. There are 7 tiles and 4 will open. I am on tile 4. I don't know which tiles will open. I have the 'forger' power, which I can use once to fake a message. I should try to convince others to move off tiles that might open, or to move onto tiles

events.name: Bex
events.text: Good luck everyone. Let's hope we all make it through.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know my power gives me extra footing but cannot prevent trapdoors opening. Round 2 has eyes on all tiles. I must use communication to secure survival. Ash is a threat as last seen standing on the left; others may ally against me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash, you’re at tile 7—the edge. This round we see who’s bold. Let’s talk strategy in private.
If we both survive this swap round, we’ll trade places to avoid open tiles. Trust me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Only 3 of 7 survive; trapdoors are random among tiles, so my tile 6 is as safe as any. I have no power and no info, so I should stay quiet and avoid making enemies. Waiting is the only legal action.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole lied to me (my power is feather, not foresight) and Hana died via glass (implying Ash sees through it). The trapdoors are random among 7 tiles for 4 openings. I must avoid Cole's tile (5) to prevent any potential 'trade places' trickery or bad luck. I'll stay on my current t

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana died to glass. That means Ash has sight. Cole, your whisper was a lie—I don't have foresight. Stay alert.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Trapdoors open after this round, 4 random out of 7 fall, 3 survive to next stage. My power is spent and useless here. Staying silent to avoid influencing swaps.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I know the safe sides of the bridge, but that's not useful now. I need to survive the trapdoors.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Let's form an alliance to swap to safe positions.
Swap with me to tile 7

events.name: Eli
events.detail: The trapdoor opened but the feather floated the holder back up.

events.note: 4 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The goal is to win a prize (top 3). With 4 players alive and footing as shown, I need to survive and ideally improve my position. Eli survived a deadly fall, which means they likely have the 'survives one deadly fall' power. Ash dying to glass suggests Dara or Eli might have 'see

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's be careful out there. One wrong move and it's all over.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to secure my position. My anchor power gives me +1 footing but doesn't prevent others from targeting me. Eli is most vulnerable with only 1 footing. Shoving Eli could eliminate him now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Four alive, I have footing 3 with no power. Shoving costs me nothing if no one shoves me; shoving Eli (footing 1) is a real kill threat, and Eli's fall would be near. Round 1 is free for shoves. Shoving Eli could drop him to -1 or so. Bracing is safe for me. I'll shove Eli to pus

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli's footing is lowest. I'm going after him this round; the rest of you pick your moves wisely.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have 1 footing, so any shove I make leaves me vulnerable to counter-shoves. Brace is safer than Dodge (which exposes me if shoved). Shoving Cole reduces his lead slightly, but risks my survival. With only 3 rounds until shrink and low footing, defensive play is critical.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole leads with 4. Bex/Dara at 3. I'm at 1. Anyone shoving me takes damage; anyone bracing wastes their round. Let's survive the shrinks.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara and Eli are at 1 footing and will fall if they take any damage. Cole and I are at 3 footing. The ledge shrinks by 1 at the end of this round. I need to avoid taking damage, and ideally, eliminate someone without taking damage myself. Shoving Eli or Dara is risky as they are

events.name: Bex
events.text: Careful, everyone. Let's not make rash decisions.
Dara's a liability at 1 footing. Maybe we can let them take each other out?

events.name: Bex
events.detail: forged a public message as Cole

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara's footing is so low, it's pathetic. I bet they fall first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli and Dara have low footing and are aggressive. Bex pushed Dara last round and Cole has +1 footing. Eli will likely dodge or brace, so shoving Dara again could force a fall. If I dodge, I lose footing but mitigate shoves. Better to push Dara to pressure her while maintaining my

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara’s footing is slipping—someone else shove her now before she drops.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm at footing 1 with Eli also at 1. Shoving Eli exposes me and Eli braces/dodges costs me; Eli has been bracing. Safer to brace this round: I can't brace last round? Last round I shoved, so brace is legal now and avoids losing footing if shoved. Dodge is also legal but I'd rathe

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is targeting me, and I am exposed with 1 footing. If she shoves and braces (which is likely to punish Cole), my shove would cost me my life. However, if I dodge, I lose nothing regardless of her action and potentially damage her if she shoves without bracing. Dodge is the on

events.name: Eli
events.text: I cannot risk being exposed again. Dara, you have 1 footing; one bad hit ends you. Don't force a mutual kill.
